title: Memory bandwidth and latency
purpose: Measure sequential, streaming and random memory throughput plus random-access latency, at working sets sized from the host's own cache topology so the result describes DRAM rather than cache.

sizing.note: The documented multiple applies to what a shape actually streams. For the single-threaded shape that is one thread's buffer; for the multi-threaded shape it is the aggregate across threads, because the threads share the last-level cache and evict each other. Each thread's slice must also exceed l2_multiple times its private L2. Sizes are clamped to max_working_set_bytes and then to memory_budget_fraction of MemAvailable divided across threads. A shape whose working set falls below min_credible_multiple times cache is reported as cache-contaminated and downgrades the result to Degraded.

preparation: Allocate one working set per thread and write every element before any timing, so page faults, zero-page sharing and NUMA first-touch placement are paid for outside the measured region. Buffers are reused across repetitions.
calibration: Per access pattern and shape, grow a probe from one pass by a bounded proportional step until a repetition exceeds a quarter of target_rep_ms, then extrapolate linearly. Capped at 2^24 passes.
warmup: warmup_reps repetitions per metric, streamed and retained but excluded from statistics.

workloads.description: Sum a DRAM-sized u64 buffer in order.
workloads.represents: Scans: log processing, full-table reads, template rendering

workloads.description: Store a per-pass value across a DRAM-sized u64 buffer.
workloads.represents: Buffer fills, response assembly, page-cache population

workloads.description: Copy between two DRAM-sized buffers via the platform memcpy. Traffic counted in both directions, STREAM Copy style.
a = b + k*c across three DRAM-sized buffers. Traffic counted as two reads plus one write, STREAM Triad style.
workloads.represents: Multi-stream traffic that saturates a memory controller

workloads.description: Independent gathers through a full-length random permutation.
workloads.represents: Hash lookups, index probes, interpreter object graphs

workloads.description: The sequential read kernel over a working set sized to half of L2.
workloads.represents: The same scan when the working set fits in cache

workloads.description: Dependent pointer chase through a Sattolo-shuffled single cycle, so no access can be prefetched or overlapped. Chunked into 65536-load passes with a cursor that persists across repetitions: a full traversal of a bandwidth-sized working set takes tens of seconds at DRAM latency, and restarting each pass from the beginning would re-walk lines already in cache.
workloads.represents: Linked structures, B-tree descent, PHP array traversal

shapes.note: latency_random has no multi shape: a threaded latency figure measures contention between cores, which is a different quantity.

derived_metrics.note: How much faster the same scan is when the working set fits in cache. Reported as context, never scored: it is a property of the cache hierarchy and a machine with a small L3 should not be penalised for it twice.

validation: Every access pattern must produce at least 5 measured repetitions.
Repetitions shorter than 20 ms are rejected as timer-noise dominated.
A shape whose working set falls below twice the last-level cache is reported as cache-contaminated and downgrades the result to Degraded.
Coefficient of variation above 0.15 raises a high-variance warning and downgrades the result to Degraded.
cleanup: None required: the module allocates only heap memory, which is released when it returns, including on cancellation.
limitations: Working sets are sized from the cache topology the host reports. Inside a container or a hypervisor that exports none, a documented default is used instead and the result records that it was assumed.

Thread placement is left to the operating system, so on a multi-socket machine the multi-threaded figures reflect default first-touch NUMA placement rather than an isolated per-node measurement. Binding threads to nodes needs privileges this module deliberately does not take.

The kernels are plain loops: no hand-written SIMD and no explicit non-temporal stores, so they measure what a normal optimised program achieves, including whatever the compiler auto-vectorises. sequential_copy is the exception - it delegates to the platform memcpy, which is what real software does and which may use non-temporal stores or other tricks the other kernels do not. That is why it can report more total traffic than a plain read of the same buffer.
Copy and Triad count traffic in both directions, as STREAM does, so their figures are roughly double and triple a one-way read of the same buffer.
Random-access latency includes TLB misses, which is what a real workload experiences but makes the figure sensitive to huge-page configuration.

scoring.note: Memory metrics carry no single_core/multi_core facet: those facets are published as core-performance numbers, and folding DRAM latency into them would change what an already-shipped score means. Reference anchors are declared targets, not measurements. See docs/SCORING-SYSTEM.md.
